record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Let X be an F-space and K a bounded subset of X. Suppose that for every open starlike set U containing 0 as an internal point, the diametral approximative quantities δ_n(K,U) tend to 0 as n -> ∞. Must K be compact?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 12T. - Let X be an F-space. Let K be a bounded set. Suppose that for each open starlike U containing 0 as an internal point 5^(K, U) ^ 0 . Is K a compact set ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be an $F$-space, i.e., a topological vector space whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. A subset $U \subseteq X$ is called starlike (with respect to $0$) if for every $x \in U$ and every $t \in [0,1]$ one has $tx \in U$; the point $0$ is an internal point of $U$ if for every $x \in X$ there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $tx \in U$ for all $t \in [-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$. For a bounded subset $K \subseteq X$, an open starlike neighborhood $U$ of $0$ with $0$ as an internal point, and an integer $n \geq 0$, define the $n$-th diametral approximative quantity
$$\delta_n(K,U) \;=\; \inf\Big\{\, t > 0 \;:\; \text{there exists a linear subspace } L \subseteq X \text{ with } \dim L \leq n \text{ such that } K \subseteq L + tU \,\Big\}.$$
Suppose that $K$ is a bounded subset of $X$ such that for every open starlike set $U \subseteq X$ containing $0$ as an internal point, one has $\delta_n(K,U) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Must $K$ be relatively compact?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source confirming a resolution of this question for general F-spaces. Related work on diametral and approximate diametral dimensions exists for nuclear Fréchet spaces and power series spaces, but no specific statement about compactness of bounded subsets of F-spaces under the stated condition was found. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Some Remarks on Diametral Dimension and Approximate Diametral Dimension of Certain Nuclear Fréchet Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies diametral dimension and approximate diametral dimension in the setting of nuclear Fréchet spaces and power series spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related research on (approximate) diametral dimension concerns nuclear Fréchet spaces, not the general F-space compactness question asked here.

status_evidence.title: Approximative dimension of a space of analytic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Approximative dimension treated in concrete function space settings.
status_evidence.claim: Literature found addresses approximative dimension but not the specific compactness implication for bounded subsets of general F-spaces.
